Notes: Provides broad climate context (e.g., humid continental vs semi-arid). Useful for regional stratification.
Description: Zonal assignment of dominant Köppen-Geiger climate class from 1 km raster (1980–2016) calculated across custom macrozones.

Notes: Reflects cold tolerance diversity; transitional zones may affect vegetation, snowmelt, soil freeze–thaw.
Description: Count of unique USDA Plant Hardiness Zones based on 30-year cold temp normals (1991–2020) calculated across custom macrozones.

Notes: Reflects dominant cold tolerance regime based on minimum winter temps. Useful for snowmelt timing, freeze–thaw effects.
Description: Zonal majority of USDA Plant Hardiness Zones based on 30-year cold temp normals (1991–2020) calculated across custom macrozones.

Effective Analytical Resolution: 1–4 sq-km, informed from 800 sq-m PRISM data
Notes: Governs evapotranspiration, freeze–thaw, snowpack formation. Baseline thermal regime.
Description: Zonal median of annual mean temperature from PRISM 1991–2020 normals, calculated across Level II ecoregions.

Effective Analytical Resolution: 1–4 sq-km, informed from 800 sq-m PRISM data
Notes: Typical annual moisture supply; important for soil moisture, runoff potential, vegetation productivity.
Description: Zonal median of total annual precipitation from PRISM 1991–2020 normals, calculated across Level II ecoregions.

Effective Analytical Resolution: 1–4 sq-km, informed from 800 sq-m PRISM data
Notes: Characterizes warm-season water input. Relevant to storm-driven systems (convective seasonality).
Description: Zonal mean percentage of total annual precipitation falling May–August from PRISM 1991–2020 normals, calculated across Level II ecoregions.

Effective Analytical Resolution: 1–4 sq-km, informed from 800 sq-m PRISM data
Notes: Captures 'typical' warm-season dominance, important for Great Plains hydrology.
Description: Zonal median percentage of total annual precipitation falling May–August from PRISM 1991–2020 normals, calculated across Level II ecoregions.

Effective Analytical Resolution: 1–4 sq-km, informed from 800 sq-m PRISM data
Notes: Captures variability across seasons. Sensitive to outliers—useful for detecting flashiness or hydrologic irregularity.
Description: Standard deviation of seasonal precip totals from PRISM 1991–2020 normals, calculated across Level III ecoregions.

Effective Analytical Resolution: 1–4 sq-km, informed from 800 sq-m PRISM data
Notes: Seasonality spread (middle 50%). Robust alternative to StDev for characterizing intra-annual precipitation variability.
Description: IQR (25th–75th percentile) of seasonal precip totals from PRISM 1991–2020 normals, calculated across Level III ecoregions.

Effective Analytical Resolution: 1–4 sq-km, informed from 800 sq-m PRISM data
Notes: Fall recharge, baseflow resetting; marks transition from convective to frontal systems.
Description: Sum of zonal medians of fall monthly precip totals (Sep–Nov) from PRISM 1991–2020 normals, calculated across Level III ecoregions.

Effective Analytical Resolution: 1–4 sq-km, informed from 800 sq-m PRISM data
Notes: Indicates snowpack formation potential and winter water storage.
Description: Sum of zonal medians of winter monthly precip (Dec–Feb) from PRISM 1991–2020 normals, calculated across Level III ecoregions.

Effective Analytical Resolution: 1–4 sq-km, informed from 800 sq-m PRISM data
Notes: Captures convective storm seasonality (flood-prone regions).
Description: Sum of zonal medians of spring monthly precip (Mar–May) from PRISM 1991–2020 normals, calculated across Level III ecoregions.

Effective Analytical Resolution: 1–4 sq-km, informed from 800 sq-m PRISM data
Notes: Key springtime recharge and flood generation season; relevant to melt-transition systems and early crop needs.
Description: Sum of zonal medians of summer monthly precip (Jun–Aug) from PRISM 1991–2020 normals, calculated across Level III ecoregions.

Notes: Captures thermally transitional zones; relevant for soil structure, infiltration disruption, and freeze–thaw runoff events.
Description: Zonal count of freeze–thaw transition days based on PRISM daily data (1991–2020), calculated across NHD+ catchments

Notes: Captures storm severity at upper tail. Correlated with flash flood potential and runoff generation efficiency.
Storm frequency and seasonal spacing. Interacts with intensity to shape hydrograph form and flood likelihood.
Dominant land cover type in agricultural basins. Reflects human land use, runoff potential, and evapotranspiration demands.
Forest cover dampens runoff and increases interception. Often associated with lower skew and more buffered hydrographs.
Grasslands moderate infiltration and evapotranspiration; especially important in mixed-use rangelands of the Plains.
Urbanized land increases imperviousness. Strong driver of peak flows and flood skew.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~250–1000 m, based on MODIS land cover fraction
Notes: Represents the dominant cover type. More interpretable than nominal class. Useful in mosaicked or fragmented landscapes.
Captures land use fragmentation, heterogeneity. May correlate with infiltration variation and complex runoff behavior.
Proportion of catchment covered by dominant land class. Useful for integrating land cover with slope, aspect, and flow.
Captures local heterogeneity within catchments. Useful for modeling land cover transitions or mixed urban–ag–grass mosaics.
Magnitude of greenness seasonal change. Indicates vigor and seasonality of vegetation response to climate.
Captures seasonal variation in greenness. IQR is robust to outliers—good for mosaic or transitional landscapes.
Number of growing-season days. Useful in hydrologic modeling for evapotranspiration or baseflow duration.
Maximum greenness during growing season. Proxy for biomass peak or vegetative productivity in humid/arid zones.
Captures broad terrain steepness across macroregions; helps distinguish dissected plains vs flat regions.
Central tendency of slope; more robust to outliers than mean. Useful in classifying runoff/infiltration dominance.
Important for capturing macroregional elevational trends that govern temperature, snow persistence, and runoff seasonality.
Description: Mean altitude of station gage, based on point location metadata, calculated across custom macrozones

Effective Analytical Resolution: Moderate resolution (5–10 km)  derived from 10 m NED
Notes: Average terrain steepness across ecoregions. Linked to stream energy, flow velocity, sediment transport.

Effective Analytical Resolution: Moderate resolution (5–10 km)  derived from 10 m NED
Notes: Asymmetry of slope distribution. Highlights dominant gentle/steep terrains; useful for detecting breaks in terrain.

Effective Analytical Resolution: Moderate resolution (5–10 km)  derived from 10 m NED
Notes: Captures slope diversity in a robust way (less sensitive to extremes). Linked to flow complexity and infiltration.

Effective Analytical Resolution: Moderate resolution (5–10 km)  derived from 10 m NED
Notes: Captures terrain variability including extremes. May signal areas of complex topography with abrupt slope changes.
Small-scale terrain heterogeneity. Linked to microrelief, runoff dispersion, ponding, and infiltration zones.
Average soil moisture tendency. Combines slope and upslope contributing area.
Most common soil moisture potential class in catchment. Helps classify dominant runoff tendency.
Categorical version of TWI to simplify terrain–moisture interactions. Improves model interpretability.
Micro-topographic heterogeneity. Proxy for infiltration potential and ponding risk.
Represents terrain steepness (catchment relief). Reflects runoff energy driving runoff potential, erosion potential, and sediment transport; and hydrograph steepness driving flashiness
Description: Zonal median elevation range (maximum minus minimum elevation) within each NHD+ catchment, based on 10 m NED data.

Notes: North–south slope orientation. +1 = north-facing; linked to solar exposure, snow persistence, and evapotranspiration rates.
Description: Zonal median of the cosine of aspect within each NHD+ catchment, derived from 10 m NED data.

Notes: East–west slope orientation. +1 = east-facing; controls early-day sun exposure, influencing melt timing and phenology.
Description: Zonal median of the sine of aspect within each NHD+ catchment, derived from 10 m NED data.

Notes: Reflects local variation in concavity/convexity as the spread of curvature values across catchment. High variability = complex terrain, mixed flow pathways, potential for localized erosion.
Description: IQR of combined curvature types across each NHD+ catchment

Notes: Detects flow convergence/divergence on hillslopes, channels (negative) and ridges (positive) linked to channel initiation, ponding, and routing divergence.
Description: Zonal median of planform (horizontal) curvature  for each NHD+ catchment, derived from 10 m NED data.

Notes: Captures slope acceleration/deceleration along flow paths. Key for identifying concave (depositional) vs convex (erosional) zones.
Description: Zonal median of profile (vertical) curvature for each NHD+ catchment, derived from 10 m NED data.

Notes: How circular a watershed is. High values = fast runoff, short lag; low values = elongated response.
Catchment shape index. Low elongation = spread out hydrograph. High elongation = flashier peaks.
Shape metric: Low = long & narrow ? delayed runoff. High = compact ? quicker hydro response. Affects peak flow shape.
Compactness of basin shape. High = more circular ? more synchronous flow, steeper hydrograph; Low = elongated ? delayed response.
Rate at which water infiltrates soil. Low permeability = high runoff potential = more positive skew.
USDA hydrologic group (A = high infiltration, D = high runoff). Linked to storm response class.
"Total stream length / area. More dissected basins respond faster; linked to runoff concentration."
"Average stream path length. Longer = slower response; shorter = rapid runoff concentration."
Gradient of the main stream path (elevation drop / length). Strongly influences runoff velocity and hydrograph steepness.

Effective Analytical Resolution: Point data used as a spatial predictor
Notes: Influences temperature regime, snow persistence, and climatic classification.
Description: Represents elevation above sea level at gage.

Notes: Relief / main channel length. Measures basin steepness and hydrologic energy. Useful for flashiness and sediment potential.
